scenes.scene_brief: Mira arrives at the storm-damaged Beacon House expecting paperwork and finds Theo boarding up the shattered lantern-room windows. Establish the salt-air setting, their ten-year almost-history, and the fact that he won the emergency stabilization contract before she knew he was bidding. End with June announcing that Mira and Theo have two weeks to submit one joint restoration plan.

Theo tries to keep the worksite professional while Mira questions every temporary brace and cost line. Show his competence, her precision, and the old hurt underneath their clipped banter. End when a fallen beam reveals water damage worse than his bid assumed.

Mira tours the inn with June and sees how much family memory is physically embedded in the building. She learns Grant Wexler has made a cash offer that would erase the inn but pay June's debts. End with Mira promising a preservation path before she knows one exists.

Theo returns to his workshop and faces payroll, supply delays, and Cal's warning that the Beacon House job could sink them. Reveal Theo's need to prove reliability. End with Theo opening the old postcard Mira sent after she left and failing to throw it away again.

At the town records office, Mira and Theo discover the original lighthouse plans are missing key pages. They must work shoulder to shoulder through dusty archives while town gossip needles them. End with Mira finding a permit note that suggests the inn has a hidden cistern.

Theo helps Mira inspect the cellar after dark. A power outage forces close quarters and honest sensory tension, but they keep consent and boundaries clear. End when they find the cistern access and realize the foundation problem may be solvable.

The heritage board says it will consider saving the Beacon House only if Mira and Theo present a fully funded plan at the Solstice Walk. Grant offers Mira an easier adaptive-reuse proposal that sidelines Theo. End with Mira choosing Theo's harder plan in public, tying their reputations together.

Theo's crew reacts badly to the expanded scope and tight deadline. Mira proposes volunteer workdays, which Theo hates because volunteers create liability. End with Theo agreeing only after Mira signs a safety protocol that proves she respects the work.

Mira and Lena discuss why Mira never came back after leaving for graduate school. Reveal that Mira thought Theo chose silence over her when she asked whether there was a reason to stay. End with Lena challenging Mira to ask him what happened instead of judging the old wound alone.

Theo catches Grant photographing structural damage for leverage. He wants to confront him, but Mira insists they document everything properly. Their conflict turns into teamwork. End with Theo noticing Mira trusts his measurements even when she argues with his conclusions.

A rain squall strands Mira and Theo inside the inn with a leaking roof and a bucket line. Let humor, competence, and physical awareness build. End when Theo wraps Mira's cut hand with careful tenderness and asks permission before touching her.

Theo tells Mira he did not answer her old stay-or-go question because his father had just abandoned the business and Theo felt trapped. He does not excuse it. End with Mira admitting his silence hurt more because she wanted him to be brave.

During a volunteer workday, Mira handles donors while Theo keeps everyone safe. After a successful repair, they share a private moment on the back stairs. Build clear mutual consent into a first kiss. End with both realizing the kiss changes the working pact.

Theo wants to define what happened, but Mira redirects into task lists. Cal warns Theo not to hide behind work again. End with Theo asking Mira for dinner after the next board prep session, using clear words.

Mira learns June's insurance payout is smaller than expected. Grant raises his offer and implies Theo's cost overruns make the restoration irresponsible. End with Mira agreeing to review both plans overnight, which Theo interprets as wavering.

Theo overreacts to Mira reviewing Grant's plan and nearly repeats the old pattern: hard work instead of honest fear. He catches himself and apologizes. End with Mira saying she needs numbers, not loyalty tests.

Mira builds a funding model using small grants, local events, and phased repairs. Show her professional brilliance and the cost of carrying every answer alone. End with her asking Theo to review the plan before she perfects it, a small act of trust.

Theo reviews Mira's funding model and adds practical savings without dismissing her vision. He reveals the shame of almost losing his crew after his father's debts. End with Mira seeing his caution as care, not cowardice.

After a long workday, Mira and Theo cook in the inn's half-functional kitchen. Let domestic ease and sensual awareness rise without explicit sex. Include verbal consent before deeper kissing. End with Mira choosing to leave before fear makes the choice for her.

Theo talks with June about the night Mira left and learns June also let Mira believe staying meant sacrifice. He understands the wound is bigger than him. End with Theo deciding the restoration plan must give Mira a future, not just a reason to stay.

A local newspaper frames Mira and Theo's partnership as a romantic reconciliation, undercutting Mira's professional credibility. She gets angry at Theo even though he did not cause it. End with Theo publicly crediting her expertise in a way that costs him the easy hero narrative.

Theo and Mira rehearse the board presentation and keep interrupting each other until they find a rhythm. The professional harmony becomes romantic charge. End with them agreeing that after the vote they will discuss what they are becoming.

The town preps for the Solstice Walk inside the unfinished inn. Mira coordinates volunteers, Theo solves a dangerous wiring issue, and the community starts to believe. End with Grant warning Mira that public affection will make the board question her objectivity.

Theo tells Mira he wants her regardless of whether she stays in Cedar Harbor permanently. This directly counters her fear of being trapped. End with Mira initiating a kiss and saying she wants one honest night without making promises she cannot keep.

Mira and Theo spend the night together off-page after clear consent and emotional honesty. Focus on the morning after: intimacy, vulnerability, and the false sense that they have solved the old wound. End with the board presentation being moved up by forty-eight hours.

Theo is quietly happy and therefore terrified. He tells Cal he is not going to push Mira to stay. Cal asks whether silence is just fear wearing better clothes. End with Theo drafting but not sending a message about what he wants.

Mira discovers a grant requirement that would force the Beacon House to operate as a community lodging program for five years. It is good for the town but complicates June's finances. End with Mira wondering whether saving the building means taking choices away from her aunt.

Theo finds evidence that Grant knew about the grant restriction and planned to use it to discredit Mira. He wants to expose Grant immediately. End with Mira insisting they need proof that will hold up in public.

Mira confesses to June that she left Cedar Harbor partly because everyone treated her ambition like a temporary rebellion. June admits she leaned on Mira too young after Mira's mother died. End with a repaired family boundary: love cannot require self-erasure.

Theo and Mira share a sensual but emotionally grounded scene in the restored keeper's room. Keep heat at sensual, consent explicit, and focus on trust rather than choreography. End with Theo almost saying love and choosing not to rush her.

The board presentation begins well until Grant introduces a surprise structural report questioning Theo's work. Mira must decide whether to defend Theo emotionally or professionally. End with her asking for a recess to inspect the report.

Theo recognizes an old subcontractor's formatting in the report and fears one of his own past shortcuts may be involved. He tells Mira the ugly possibility before she finds it. End with Mira staying beside him because honesty came before proof.

Mira proves Grant's report is misleading but also uncovers a real permit gap from Theo's early career. The board postpones the vote. End with Mira furious that Theo's past mistake gave Grant a weapon.

Theo explains the permit gap without minimizing it: he was young, overwhelmed, and wrong. He accepts whatever professional consequence comes. End with Mira saying accountability matters but trust has been damaged.
Grant offers a compromise: he will preserve the lighthouse facade if Mira publicly withdraws Theo's plan. It would save her reputation and break Theo's. End with Mira asking for one night to decide.

Theo learns Mira is considering Grant's compromise and assumes she has chosen control over trust. He withdraws his crew to protect them from liability, effectively dooming the timeline. End with Mira seeing the empty worksite and believing Theo left again when it mattered.

Mira works alone through the inn and realizes both she and Theo recreated the old wound: she planned without trusting him; he acted without explaining. End with June refusing to let Mira confuse self-reliance with wisdom.

Theo visits his father, not for reconciliation but to stop letting inherited failure define him. He names the pattern: when scared, he disappears into work or withdrawal. End with Theo deciding to repair publicly, even if Mira does not forgive him.

Mira convenes Lena, June, Cal, and local business owners to build a transparent rescue plan. She asks for help directly for the first time. End with the group agreeing to a public repair marathon before the final vote.

Theo returns to the inn before dawn, not to take over but to ask what Mira needs and state what he can safely offer. Their apology is incomplete but real. End with Mira allowing him back onto the plan under transparent terms.

The repair marathon begins. Show community members choosing the inn over Grant's money for specific, practical reasons. End with Mira finding the missing original plan pages inside an old chart drawer.

The original plan pages reveal a cheaper code-compliant solution, but installing it before the vote is risky. Theo refuses to gamble with safety. End with Mira backing his call publicly, proving trust under pressure.

Mira and Theo spend a long night documenting the revised plan for the board. Their attraction is present but they prioritize the work and their repaired communication. End with Mira telling Theo she wants a future that includes leaving and returning by choice.
Theo says he loves Mira and does not attach the declaration to any demand that she stay. Make this a calm, earned truth rather than a plea. End with Mira not saying it back yet but staying present.

Grant makes one final offer directly to June, promising immediate debt relief. June wavers because she is tired. Mira must honor June's agency instead of forcing the preservation outcome. End with June choosing the community plan because it now has real numbers, not nostalgia.

Theo's grand gesture is practical and public: he accepts formal responsibility for the old permit gap, offers a transparent warranty structure, and protects Mira's plan from being dismissed as romance-driven. End with Mira realizing he has chosen accountability over image.

At the final heritage-board meeting, Mira presents the revised plan and refuses both nostalgia and fear. The board challenges financing, safety, and community use. End with the deciding vote tied and the board chair asking June to speak as owner.

June speaks for the inn as a living business, not a shrine. Theo watches Mira accept praise without deflecting. The board approves the plan. End with Grant leaving defeated but not cartoonish, and the work truly beginning.

Weeks later, the Beacon House opens its first restored rooms for the harbor apprenticeship fundraiser. Resolve June's finances, Lena's cafe partnership, and Cal's crew stability. End with Mira finding Theo in the lantern room where everything began.

In the lantern room, Mira says she loves Theo and names the future she is choosing: work that may take her away sometimes, a home she returns to, and a relationship built on speaking before fear acts. Close with a grounded HEA: the beacon lit, the inn saved, and both characters choosing each other freely.
